prompt: At Summer's annual physical exam on May 31st, her height was determined to be 4 feet and 3 inches. Summer last visited the doctor the previous year on September 28th at which time her height was 3 feet and $11\frac12$ inches. Based on this data, on average, how many inches did Summer grow each day? (February had 28 days.) Express your answer as a common fraction.

solutions.title: Growth ÷ days
solutions.body:
Growth: from 3 ft $11\frac12$ in to 4 ft 3 in is $\frac12 + 3 = 3\frac12$ inches.
Days: Sept 28 → 30 is 2 days, then Oct 31, Nov 30, Dec 31, Jan 31, Feb 28, Mar 31, Apr 30, May 31: $2 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 28 + 31 + 30 + 31 = 245$.
Rate: $\frac{7}{2} \div 245 = \frac{7}{490} = \frac{1}{70}$ inch per day.

**Answer: $\frac{1}{70}$ inch per day**

solutions.title: Count days backward
solutions.body:
A full year minus the days from May 31 to Sept 28: there are $30 + 31 + 31 + 28 = 120$ days from May 31 to Sept 28, so $365 - 120 = 245$ days from Sept 28 to May 31. Heights in inches: $47.5 \to 51$, a growth of 3.5. $\frac{3.5}{245} = \frac{1}{70}$.

**Answer: $\frac{1}{70}$ inch per day**

prompt: At Summer's last doctor visit on September 28 her height was 3 feet $11\frac12$ inches, and at her annual physical exam on May 31st (the following year, not a leap year) her height was 4 feet 3 inches. Summer wants to ride the Shocker roller coaster before returning to school. Unfortunately, this roller coaster has a minimum height restriction of $4\frac12$ ft. Summer measured herself on August 16th, and she is still not tall enough. If Summer maintained her average rate of growth between those two doctor visits since May 31st, how many inches does Summer need to grow during the rest of her summer break in order to meet the minimum height restriction and ride the Shocker? Express your answer as a mixed number in simplest form.

solutions.title: Growth since May 31
solutions.body:
Average rate: $3\frac12$ in over 245 days (Sept 28 to May 31) $= \frac1{70}$ in/day.
May 31 → Aug 16: $30 + 31 + 16 = 77$ days, growth $\frac{77}{70} = 1\frac1{10}$ in. Height: 4 ft $4\frac1{10}$ in. Needed: $4$ ft $6$ in, so $6 - 4\frac1{10} = 1\frac9{10}$ inches more.

**Answer: $1\frac{9}{10}$ inches**

solutions.title: All in inches
solutions.body:
Required height $54$ in. Height Aug 16: $51 + 77 \cdot \frac1{70} = 51 + 1.1 = 52.1$ in. Needed: $54 - 52.1 = 1.9 = 1\frac9{10}$ in.

**Answer: $1\frac{9}{10}$ inches**

prompt: At Summer's last doctor visit on September 28 her height was 3 feet $11\frac12$ inches, and at her annual physical exam on May 31st (the following year, not a leap year) her height was 4 feet 3 inches. The Shocker roller coaster has a minimum height restriction of $4\frac12$ ft. Assume Summer keeps growing at her average rate between those two doctor visits. Summer is determined to ride the Shocker before school begins on September 8th. Summer heard that practicing yoga makes you taller. In addition to the number of inches Summer expects to grow from August 16th to September 7th, by how many inches will Summer need to increase her height as a result of practicing yoga in order to meet the minimum height restriction and ride the Shocker before September 8th? Express your answer as a mixed number in simplest form.

solutions.title: Step by step
solutions.body:
Rate: $3\frac12$ in over 245 days $= \frac1{70}$ in/day.
Height on Aug 16: $51 + \frac{77}{70} = 52\frac1{10}$ in (77 days after May 31). She still needs $54 - 52\frac1{10} = 1\frac9{10}$ in.
Aug 16 → Sept 7: $15 + 7 = 22$ days, natural growth $\frac{22}{70} = \frac{11}{35}$ in.
Yoga must add $1\frac9{10} - \frac{11}{35} = \frac{133}{70} - \frac{22}{70} = \frac{111}{70} = 1\frac{41}{70}$ in.

**Answer: $1\frac{41}{70}$ inches**

solutions.title: Directly from May 31
solutions.body:
May 31 → Sept 7 is $30 + 31 + 31 + 7 = 99$ days, growth $\frac{99}{70}$ in. She needs $54 - 51 = 3$ in total, so yoga must add $3 - \frac{99}{70} = \frac{111}{70} = 1\frac{41}{70}$ in.

**Answer: $1\frac{41}{70}$ inches**
